sections.h2: Who to call about a Nicholas County tax bill
sections.html:
Everything runs through the courthouse at 125 East Main Street in Carlisle. The PVA (the county's property valuation office) is in the basement, answers at 859-289-3735 and keeps hours from 8:30 to 4:30 on weekdays. The Sheriff's Office, at 859-289-3740, collects what is owed.

Mail to the PVA goes to P.O. Box 2, Carlisle, KY 40311. The PVA website carries the certified tax roll, a tax estimator, forms and a fee schedule. Because the sheriff only collects, a dispute about a figure starts with the PVA, and a question about where to send a payment starts with the sheriff.

If you plan to sell, make both calls early. Ask the PVA how the parcel is classed and what value is on the roll, and ask the sheriff whether every year is paid. Two short calls tell you most of what a title agent will want to know.

Nicholas is one of Kentucky's smallest and most rural counties, and Carlisle is the seat. Few people move in or out in a given year, and new construction is rare, so most sales are of existing houses. In so small a county, a handful of sales can swing the averages.

  • Population is 7,949 for July 2025, up 5.5% from the 2020 base.
  • There are 3,355 housing units, and only 3 building permits were issued in 2025.
  • Owners occupy 74.5% of homes.
  • The midpoint value of an owned house is $123,000.
  • Monthly owner costs are $1,143 with a mortgage and $426 without.
  • Gross rent has a midpoint of $728, and household income a midpoint of $59,531.

Many local properties are farms or homes with a trade or small business attached. A seller with acreage should ask the PVA how land, barns and the house are classed on the roll before comparing values with a neighbor's.

Bills go out around October 1 each year, and payment follows KRS 134.015.

Nicholas County bill totals under the state due-date statute
Date paidConsequence
No later than November 1Two percent off the total
November 2 through year endThe total printed on the bill
During JanuaryFive percent added
Past January 31Ten percent added

The statute stops at 10%, but some Kentucky sheriffs post a higher charge for the stretch between February and mid-April. Call 859-289-3740 for the figure that applies on your payment date.

The same statute makes the tax, fees, penalties and interest a personal debt of the taxpayer from the assessment date until it is paid. If you are closing near a deadline, ask the sheriff for a written payoff rather than relying on the bill alone.

You cannot skip the first step: sit down with the Nicholas County PVA or a deputy. KRS 133.120 makes that conference a prerequisite, and it can happen before or during the inspection window or an extension of it. Staff lay out the rules and how they got your number, and the office keeps a note of the talk.

Under KRS 133.045 the roll stays open for inspection for 13 days from the first Monday in May. If you still disagree afterward, hand the County Clerk a letter or petition naming the parcel, your reasons and what you think fair cash value is. It is due the next workday after inspection ends, and you may make an audio recording when the county hears your case.

Bring evidence: recent sales of similar houses, repair estimates, photos of condition problems. Filing never postpones payment. You pay on your stated value, and the final value decides what else is owed, with interest.

A homeowner who is 65 or older, or who a federal agency or retirement system has classed as totally disabled, can claim a state deduction of $49,100 for tax years 2025 and 2026. File at the PVA in the courthouse basement. Disability claims must be renewed each year. Owners with a service-connected disability, and those found permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or the state retirement system, are exempt from that renewal.

The deduction is personal. A buyer who qualifies has to apply on their own after the sale.

sections.h2: Who receives the bill after a purchase?
sections.html:
Value and ownership are both fixed as of January 1. Someone who buys later in the year does not get billed until the following calendar year, so the earlier owner receives that bill. The PVA tries to mail a copy to the buyer using information from a tax agreement signed by buyer or seller. A buyer who receives none can get a copy from the sheriff at 859-289-3740.

  • Seller: confirm the current bill is paid and keep the receipt.
  • Buyer: have a mailing address entered on the deed, as KRS 382.135 requires.
  • Both: put the year's tax split into the contract.
  • Estate sales: the executor lists heirs and estimated values in an affidavit at the County Clerk's office.

A sale does not wipe out unpaid tax. KRS 134.420 lets the lien from a delinquent bill last up to eleven years, attached to the parcel no matter who owns it. If you think an old year might still be open, ask the sheriff before you list, because the buyer's title agent will ask the same question.

  1. Ask the sheriff for a payoff covering every open year.
  2. Pay it at or before closing so the lien can be released.
  3. Keep the receipt and hand a copy to the closing agent.
  4. Settle the current year's share in the contract.

A cash sale skips bank underwriting and repair demands, but the tax lien still has to be cleared at the table. With very few new houses being built, most buyers here are weighing older homes, so a clean tax record is one less thing to negotiate.

sections.h2: Before you list a Nicholas County house
sections.html:
Gather a few papers before the first showing. Start with this year's tax bill and proof it was paid. Look up your parcel on the PVA's certified tax roll and check the owner name, acreage and classification. If the name on the roll differs from the name on the deed, the PVA can sort that out, and it is easier to do before a buyer is waiting.

Next, decide how the year's tax will be split. Because the owner on January 1 is billed for the whole year, a seller who closes in spring or summer usually credits the buyer for the months the buyer will own the house. Write that split into the contract so the title agent can follow it. If the property is an estate, gather the executor's paperwork and plan on the affidavit of heirs and values at the County Clerk's office.

Finally, call the sheriff once more a few days before closing. Payment records can lag, and a fresh payoff figure on the day is worth the two minutes it takes.

faqs.q: Where is the Nicholas County PVA?
faqs.a: The PVA works from the courthouse basement at 125 East Main Street in Carlisle, with weekday hours from 8:30 to 4:30 and a phone at 859-289-3735.

faqs.q: Who gets a Nicholas County bill after the house sells?
faqs.a: The previous owner is billed until the next calendar year, and the PVA tries to mail a copy to the buyer. A buyer with none can call the sheriff at 859-289-3740.

faqs.q: How much does paying early save in Nicholas County?
faqs.a: Two percent, if the whole bill is paid by November 1. After that the printed total is due through December 31.

faqs.q: What penalty follows January in Nicholas County?
faqs.a: KRS 134.015 sets 5% for January and 10% after January 31. Ask the sheriff for the exact payoff, since a higher late charge may apply in late winter and spring.

faqs.q: What does the homestead exemption remove in Nicholas County?
faqs.a: The state takes $49,100 off assessed value once a qualifying owner applies at the PVA. Qualifying means 65 or over, or totally disabled, and the figure covers tax years 2025 and 2026.
